html:
Spanish Sahara was the Spanish colony on the Atlantic coast of north-west Africa from 1884 to 1976, the land now called Western Sahara. The map shows it from 1914 to 1938.

It was made of two parts: Río de Oro in the south and Saguia el-Hamra in the north. It was mostly desert, home to Sahrawi nomads, and for a long time Spain held only a few coastal posts. In 1958, after the Ifni War with newly independent Morocco, Spain made it a province. Large phosphate deposits found at Bou Craa in the 1940s and 1960s made it worth more.

In the 1970s the UN pressed Spain to leave, and the Polisario Front fought for Sahrawi independence. Morocco and Mauritania claimed the land. As Franco lay dying in 1975, Morocco sent 350,000 unarmed marchers across the border in the Green March. Spain handed the territory to Morocco and Mauritania and left in early 1976, without the vote on independence the Sahrawis had been promised.
sum: Spanish Sahara was the Spanish colony on the Atlantic coast of north-west Africa from 1884 to 1976, the land now called Western Sahara. The map shows it from 1914 to 1938.
